entries.proposition: Design: female wild-type, C3-knockout and C4B-knockout mice only (chosen because wild-type females are more seizure-prone at the subconvulsant dose), PTZ at 80 or 50 mg/kg, 10-minute video scoring.
entries.snippet: We used only female animals in our studies since it was shown that WT females are more susceptible to seizures than males in case of subconvulsant (50–60 mg/kg) dosage of PTZ

experimental_context.system: female C57BL/6 wild-type, C3-/- and C4B-/- mice, 8-12 weeks, PTZ 80 or 50 mg/kg, n = 4-6 per group
experimental_context.genotype: constitutive C3-/- and C4B-/- versus wild type
experimental_context.endpoint: seizure score and mortality, cortical IEG/cytokine mRNA at 9 min, Egr1 protein, rotarod and Barnes maze

entries.proposition: Primary result at 80 mg/kg: C4B-null mice reach scores 5-6 and 100 percent mortality (6 of 6) against none in wild type; C3-null have lower scores (2-3), one of six dying at 28 minutes.
entries.snippet: C4B-deficient mice had very severe seizures with maximal epileptic scores of 5–6 developed within 10 min period post-PTZ administration (Figure 1B), and 100% mortality rate within 6–12 min period post-PTZ-administration (Table 2).

entries.proposition: At the 50 mg/kg subconvulsant dose C4B-null mice reached scores 5-6 with 60 percent mortality (3 of 5), against wild type and C3-null at 0-1 and 0 percent (n = 5).
entries.snippet: However, C4B-deficient mice developed severe seizures with ∼100 s latency to score 3 or above (Figure 1C), maximal epileptic scores 5–6 (Figure 1D), and a 60% mortality rate (Table 2).

entries.snippet: However, our study shows only association of behavior problems in C4-deficient mice with low level of Erg1 expression in the CNS.
